players.product: AI-Native Cloud: inference cloud (Inference Engine, serverless inference) and GPU Droplets on NVIDIA HGX and AMD Instinct GPUs, integrated with its Core Cloud

quarterly_data.signal: Inference Engine (CEO): the inference platform went GA slightly less than 4 months ago and now has 'a lot more than 6,000 customers'; of the 6,000 announced in August only a handful came through direct sales - about 99% came through product-led, try-then-buy adoption. DigitalOcean introduced a feature called model synthesis, in which several models work on the same task in real time and the module stitches the answer together, alongside model routing. CEO: the front door to the platform is moving from 'give me a GPU' to 'I want tokens of this flavor', after which customers expand into agents, storage and databases; DigitalOcean's AI-Native Cloud has 5 layers.
quarterly_data.figure: a lot more than 6,000 Inference Engine customers; about 99% via product-led growth

quarterly_data.signal: ARR per megawatt (CFO): DigitalOcean generated $22 million of ARR per megawatt in Q2, and on an incremental basis it is 30%-40% higher than what neoclouds achieve, which the CFO puts at $9 million to $10 million on an embedded base (high single digits, maybe getting to 10 or 11), because of inference services and Core Cloud pull-through. The incremental figure of 13 it gave earlier was based on Q4 2025 numbers and mix; since then the mix has improved, new services add levers and pricing has increased - H100 and H200 pricing is going up, not down. DigitalOcean does not guide ARR per megawatt. Drivers: newer GPU generations make more tokens per megawatt at higher CapEx per megawatt but a very similar return; more Core Cloud attach and higher-layer services instead of bare metal; and token-yield optimization - selling tokens at a materially higher price on roughly 60% utilization, with the aim of lifting it to 70% to 80% through traffic from other regions and off-hours batch inference.
quarterly_data.figure: $22 million ARR per megawatt in Q2; incremental 30%-40% above neoclouds; token utilization roughly 60%, aiming for 70% to 80%

quarterly_data.signal: Data center and GPU suppliers (CFO): DigitalOcean works with tier 1 data center providers - Equinix, DataBank and QTS - which has let it turn up data centers on time and even ahead of schedule, and it is sourcing incremental space effectively; tier 1 providers see it as a diversified, profitable customer with a better yield than hyperscalers. 'From a GPU standpoint, we have tremendous relationships with both NVIDIA and AMD.'

Margin dynamics of the build-out (CFO): adding capacity pressures gross margin and, to a lesser degree, EBITDA margin, because a new data center's lease expense hits right away and the equipment - which DigitalOcean tends to finance and pay for over time - is depreciated as soon as it ships; operating leverage holds up because people and OpEx do not grow at the rate of revenue. The CFO said margin pressure will continue as long as DigitalOcean keeps growing and bringing on data centers, and that it should keep investing while it earns its current returns.
